render.implementation: (1) THE BOARD: VLM roster keyframes every 4 frames (17 keyframes, batch-1's pixel-format corruption re-run clean) + the dedicated per-frame fine ball pass f050-f064 + a top-band LK/RANSAC camera path, all fused by an ANCHORED solve (scipy least_squares: a shear-affine world model world=A@frame+cam(t) constrained by the goal-mouth world constancy, the ball's net endpoint, the GK at his post, the shooter ending in front of the goal, the ball never past the line pre-shot) — the pure-translation v1 and free-poly v2 were measured (world span 37-1743, the ball past the goal pre-shot) and honestly refused; outlier pass + PCHIP + MA(5) densify to 65 frames; deterministic OpenCV render (mow-stripe pitch, penalty box, goal net box, numbered markers, ball trail, GOAL pulse) + ffmpeg x264 8fps. (2) THE CLARITY: fastNlMeansDenoisingColored(h=4) + unsharp(sigma 1.4, amount 0.7 anime / 1.2 3d) on every frame of the propagated outputs — A/B VLM-gated (the anime strong measured crunchy and refused). (3) THE BALL: per-frame cut-and-paste f052-f064 — the anime's own patterned ball disc cut from the verified stuck/teleported positions (Hough CIRCLE-ON-BALL + crop-verified), pasted at the source's tracked flight positions; the vacated sites filled with mid-tone annulus grass + the pitch lines REDRAWN from the originals' fitted lines (the v1 TELEA smear, the v2 bright-fill, the v3 dark-median, the v4 donor-clone were each measured at crop level and refused — the line-preserving v5 passed CLEAN at full-frame scale).

designGate.method: check BEFORE freezing, never after: the flicker metric (region y420-620 x540-740, mean |luminance jump| per frame), the strict VLM ball-count at MERGED-CROP level (the full-frame pass double-counted the same ball across split crops — disproven by merged-crop checks, honestly typed), the crop-verified ball-trajectory checks (true positions + vacated sites + lines), the six-question board check, the A/B clarity gate, the five-question overall check
designGate.ballCheck: the merged-crop strict count across the shot window (c053/c055 wide crops + the c053/c055 quadrant battery + the c058/c061/c064 true-position/vacated-site pairs): every frame exactly ONE patterned ball — MAX: 1 (the full-frame VLM count reported 2 at c053/c055 and 0 at the net frames — both disproven at crop level: the split-crop boundary double-counted the same ball, and the net-area ball is small at full-frame scale but crop-verified PRESENT)
designGate.ballTrajectory: the anime ball now LEAVES the shooter at the strike (f052) and follows the source's own fine-pass flight to the net (f062-64): crop-verified at the true positions 3/3 BALL-PRESENT + CLEAN; the vacated feet sites CLEAN with the pitch lines redrawn continuous (v7 full-frame check: 3/3 CLEAN); the teleported-goal ball also moved to the true net position
designGate.boardCheck: the six-question VLM check on spread board frames (b001/b013/b025/b041/b053/b064): (1) a 2D top-down pitch with field lines YES (2) player markers whose positions change across frames YES (3) a white ball marker YES (4) the ball travels to the right-side goal and ends in the net YES (5) the overall animation reads as an attacking play ending in a goal YES (6) no visual defects YES — 6/6

clarity.abVerdict: A/B VLM: anime ships MILD (the strong measured crunchy edges on the line art — refused); 3d ships STRONG ('looks like a higher-resolution render, minimal to no artifacts')

designGate.overallVerdict: A) YES, the same goal-play event (dribble, shot, goal) is identifiable across all ten spread frames. B) YES, images 1-3 are a 2D overhead pitch with numbered circular markers for players and a dot for the ball. C) YES, images 4-6 are a clean 3D game-engine render style. D) YES, images 7-10 are hand-drawn anime with the ball flying into the net after the shot. E) YES, each version keeps a consistent style without mixing.
